data.narrative:
Stoke Space, founded by Andy Lapsa and Tom Feldman, is a Series D-stage space and aerospace company that has raised $860M to date. The valuation assessment draws from a comparable universe of 4 private peers at Series C and D stages, as well as 5 public Space & Aerospace companies (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL).

Two valuation methods triangulate a defensible range. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.5x step-up multiplier to the $860M raised proxy, implying $1.3B. Peer-median analysis across 4 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—Sierra Space ($8.0B), Apex Space ($2.3B), Varda Space Industries ($1.5B), and Skyryse ($1.1B)—yields a median of $1.9B, with a range from $1.1B to $8.0B. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples (23.9x median across the sector) cannot be applied without disclosed revenue.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $1.1B to $2.2B, with a median of $1.6B. Key uncertainties include the wide dispersion in peer valuations (particularly the $8.0B outlier for Sierra Space), the absence of revenue disclosure limiting public-market anchoring, and the relatively small private peer sample. Stage-progression and peer-median methods show material divergence ($1.3B vs. $1.9B), reflecting inherent uncertainty in early-stage aerospace valuations.
